name: PWW World Championship
epitaph: The PWW's main title through the 1997-2001 run. Its January 1999 broadcast has Johnny Blaze carrying it as champion after taking it from Congo, with a rematch set for Winter Warzone on 7 February, and the federation's own later account names Jay Phoenix as a two-time holder and the only man ever to hold every PWW title.
notes: Named in the federation's own account of its own history on the 2004 staff page (/promotions/pww-worldwide-1999/archive/staff-2004.html), which lists the five titles of the 1997-2001 run. The revival's four divisions are filed as their own rows; nothing held states whether they continued these belts. The 1999 broadcast is the only held document that stages a reign of it (/promotions/pww-worldwide-1999/archive/pww-wednesday-night-wildfire-1999-01-21.html).

name: PWW Intercontinental Championship
epitaph: One of the five titles of the PWW's 1997-2001 run. Nothing held records a single reign of it beyond the federation's own statement that Jay Phoenix held it, and most of them more than once.
notes: Named in the federation's own account of its own history on the 2004 staff page (/promotions/pww-worldwide-1999/archive/staff-2004.html), which lists the five titles of the 1997-2001 run. name: Chris Williams Television Championship
epitaph: The PWW's television title, named for Chris Williams, a PWW executive killed in a road accident on 4 May 1999. It is the belt the community's own Chris Williams Memorial Cup grew out of: the Cup's own roll of winners dates the tournament "right back to the first ever tournament to crown what was then called the Chris Williams Television Title (over at PWW)." Jay Phoenix held it among the five.
notes: Named in the federation's own account of its own history on the 2004 staff page (/promotions/pww-worldwide-1999/archive/staff-2004.html), which lists the five titles of the 1997-2001 run. The revival's four divisions are filed as their own rows; nothing held states whether they continued these belts. The CWTV abbreviation is the staff page's own; the expansion and the tournament origin are the Chris Williams Memorial Cup roll's own words, from the Primetime Central forum (post 230294, workshop-held). Chris Williams is on the memorial register.

name: PWW Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The tag title of the PWW's 1997-2001 run. Nothing held records a reign of it beyond the federation's own statement that Jay Phoenix held it.
notes: Named in the federation's own account of its own history on the 2004 staff page (/promotions/pww-worldwide-1999/archive/staff-2004.html), which lists the five titles of the 1997-2001 run. name: PWW Eternal Championship
epitaph: The main title of the PWW's 2004 reopening — "the pinnacle of a wrestler's achievement," in the federation's own words, defended once a month. The reopening never staged a show, and the belt has no recorded holder.
notes: Named as the Eternal division (world) on the federation's own 2004 rulebook (/promotions/pww-worldwide-1999/archive/rules-2004.html) and listed as a championship on its own front page of 25 November 2003 (/promotions/pww-worldwide-1999/archive/front-page-2003-11-25.html). Whether it continued the PWW World Championship of the 1997-2001 run is not stated anywhere held.

name: PWW Shooting Star Championship
epitaph: The PWW's starting title at the 2004 reopening, open to the whole roster and defended every week — "the first title on the road to the World title," and no less important for it, the federation said. It has no recorded holder.
notes: Named as the Shooting Star division (television) on the federation's own 2004 rulebook (/promotions/pww-worldwide-1999/archive/rules-2004.html), which describes it as similar to a television title in other federations, and listed on the front page of 25 November 2003. Whether it continued the Chris Williams Television Championship is not stated anywhere held.

name: PWW Nightmare Championship
epitaph: The hardcore title of the PWW's 2004 reopening — tables, falls count anywhere, no disqualification — defendable, in the federation's own words, anytime, anyplace. It has no recorded holder.
notes: Named as the Nightmare division (hardcore / extreme) on the federation's own 2004 rulebook (/promotions/pww-worldwide-1999/archive/rules-2004.html) and listed on the front page of 25 November 2003.

name: PWW Gemini Championship
epitaph: The tag title of the PWW's 2004 reopening, open both to two singles wrestlers pairing up and to a handler running a team of his own, and defended every two weeks. It has no recorded holder.
notes: Named as the Gemini division (tag) on the federation's own 2004 rulebook (/promotions/pww-worldwide-1999/archive/rules-2004.html) and listed on the front page of 25 November 2003. Whether it continued the PWW Tag Team Championship of the 1997-2001 run is not stated anywhere held.

name: Master of the Mat
epitaph: The PWW's own annual single-elimination tournament, open to the whole roster, whose winner claimed the title of Master of the Mat — an accolade rather than a belt, never defended. Its second annual running was the federation's pay-per-view of 14 November 1999, and the reopening of 2004 kept it on the calendar. Jay Phoenix is the one winner the surviving record names.
notes: Set out in the federation's own 2004 rulebook (/promotions/pww-worldwide-1999/archive/rules-2004.html): "Once a year, there will also be a single elimination style tournament, open to the whole roster, the winner of which will be able to claim the title of 'Master of the Mat'. This is not an official belt, but is rather an accolade, and will not be defended." The 1999 running is the federation's own second annual, held as a pay-per-view broadcast from the Sky Dome, Toronto — collected, not served. Jay Phoenix's win is named on the 2004 staff page (/promotions/pww-worldwide-1999/archive/staff-2004.html), without a year.
